claims.text: High-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings from 300 to 700 °C is predominantly controlled by the formation and stability of an adherent multicomponent oxide scale.
An adherent oxide layer reduces direct metal-to-metal contact.
The oxide layer mitigates abrasive wear.
HVOF or cold spraying can be used as conventional deposition methods for this coating.
The undoped starting coating has a fine microstructure.
The undoped starting coating has only limited oxide formation under ambient conditions.
The proposed intervention is addition of 1–2 at.% Y to FeNiCrCoCu.
The proposed wear tests span 300–700 °C and contact loads of 10–100 MPa.
Sufficient oxygen can drive formation of mixed metal-oxide surface films in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed scale comprises oxides of Fe, Ni, Cr, Co, and Cu and may incorporate yttrium oxide.
Reactive-element doping and optimized oxygen partial pressure make the oxide scale more uniform and adherent.
Yttrium promotes oxidation kinetics that favor formation of a cohesive and protective oxide layer.
Mixed metal-oxide surface films tend to reduce wear rates in high-entropy alloys.
A protective oxide layer formed during thermal exposure can enhance wear resistance of a related high-entropy-alloy coating.
The stable oxide barrier lowers friction under high-temperature, high-load conditions.
Y-doped FeNiCrCoCu tested in oxygen-enriched conditions will form a more uniform and adherent scale than the undoped baseline.
Y-doped FeNiCrCoCu tested in oxygen-enriched conditions will have a lower wear rate than the undoped baseline.
Y-doped FeNiCrCoCu tested in oxygen-enriched conditions will have a lower friction coefficient than the undoped baseline.
The mechanism is applicable throughout 300–700 °C and 10–100 MPa for thin protective coatings.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome says the Y-doped, oxygen-enriched coating is compared with the undoped baseline under identical conditions, but the baseline is explicitly assigned standard ambient oxygen while the intervention includes elevated oxygen partial pressure. Thus the stated comparison is not under identical atmospheric conditions and confounds Y addition with oxygen enrichment.
